faq.a: Yaqoub is associated with the Arabic form يَعْقُوب, whose core sense is yaqoub; jacob (prophet).

faq.q: What is the origin of Yaqoub?
faq.a: Yaqoub is associated with Arabic. Yaqoub is Arabic يَعْقُوب (Yaʿqūb), the Quranic form of the prophet Jacob.
Yes — the underlying form يَعْقُوب is Arabic.
Yaqoub can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Yaqoub should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Yaʿqūb is the Quranic Arabic form of the prophet Jacob and occurs in the Quran.

faq.a: In Urdu, Yaqoub is rendered یعقوب and carries the sense یعقوب، نبی کا نام.

faq.q: What does Yaqoub mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Yaqoub is rendered یعقوب and carries the sense یعقوب، نام پیامبر.
A romanized syllable approximation is ya-qoub. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Yaqoub, yaqoub. Script forms are يَعْقُوب, یعقوب, याक़ूब.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
